description: Equipo multidisciplinario, creemos en el uso de las nuevas tecnologias para solucionar y resolver problemas de manera innovadoras
summary: We aim to bridge the gap between technical aerospace science and the general public through interactive media. By making players experience the direct consequences of engineering choices, we hope to inspire a deep appreciation for the meticulous planning and teamwork behind real NASA missions. Moving forward, we hope to expand the game with more modular spacecraft components, dynamic multi-mission campaigns, and broader VR hardware compatibility.
details:
The core gameplay relies on a zero-sum, cause-and-effect loop divided into two main phases:

  1. The Assembly Phase: The Ground Control (PC) player builds the spacecraft on a strict budget. They must choose components across four subsystems (Power, Life Support, Communications, and Payload).
  2. The Execution Phase: The Commander (VR) pilots the ship. The catch is that the VR player's crises are directly caused by Ground Control's design choices. If the PC player bought a cheap life-support system to save money, it triggers physical crisis minigames in the VR cockpit (like sudden oxygen leaks or power overloads).

Because the VR player cannot see the flight manuals, and Ground Control cannot see the cockpit, they must communicate flawlessly to survive. To facilitate this under pressure, the VR cockpit uses industrial, color-coded NASA acronyms (ECLSS, PWR, COMM) and an analog "status light" feedback loop where the VR player must physically confirm when a system is fixed.

What benefits does it have? The project translates highly complex aerospace engineering concepts—such as mass-to-fuel ratios, Debris Avoidance Maneuvers (DAM), and Keep-Out Sphere (KOS) protocols—into an accessible, adrenaline-fueled experience. Instead of reading about space physics in a textbook, players actively experience the stress and consequences of engineering trade-offs. It strongly fosters teamwork, active listening, and problem-solving under extreme pressure.
